title: Islanded node recovery playbook + triage scratchpad
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Working notes to capture an operator-friendly recovery flow for 'islanded' nodes: nodes that have lost sufficient control-plane / CNI connectivity such that scheduling, readiness, or ingress traffic is effectively blocked despite node being technically "Ready".
- Intended audience: on-call SRE, platform engineers, and pager responders.

Short summary (one sentence):
- On 2025-02-11 03:47 UTC we observed a region-wide spike of pods stuck in Pending and LB 5xxs; investigation pointed to a subset of nodes that had degraded CNI dataplane and intermittent kubelet->apiserver flakiness — nodes became "islanded" (control-plane reachable intermittently, data-plane to other nodes broken).

Symptoms observed:
- Large increase in pods Pending (scheduler logs show repeated backoff due to resource accounting mismatches).
- Flaky L4/L7 for services with endpoints on affected nodes (TCP RSTs, connection timeouts).
- kubelet logs: repeated error "unable to update status: timed out waiting for the condition" and bursts of TLS handshake errors to apiserver.
- CNI daemon (calico) logs show BPF sync failures and frequent netlink errors.
- Node metrics: high tx-err/tx-drop on eth0, conntrack table near high-watermark on affected nodes.

Detection rules (alerts we should tune):
- Alert if >5% of nodes in a cluster have tx_drop_rate > 0.5% for 5m.
- Alert if API server 5xx rate to kubelets increases >200% p95 for 1m.
- Alert if pod Pending count for >10m increases by more than 50 in a zone.
- Add an "islanded-node" anomaly rule that correlates: node Ready==True but kubelet-heartbeat|apiserver RTT > 1s and podEndpointLoss > 30% on node.

Timeline (trimmed):
- 2025-02-11 03:40 UTC: first LB 5xx page from customer.
- 03:47 UTC: SRE on-call acknowledges. 03:52 UTC: Pager shows spike in Pending pods.
- 04:00 UTC: triage finds group of 7 nodes in us-east-1a with high tx_drop and repeated calico errors.
- 04:10 UTC: temporary mitigation applied: cordon + migrate stateful non-critical pods off two worst nodes.
- 04:22 UTC: reconfigure conntrack thresholds as stop-gap (see mitigation commands).
- 04:50 UTC: rolling restart of calico-node on affected nodes; kubelet restarts scheduled if recovery not seen.
- 05:30 UTC: majority of nodes recovered, pending pods drained and scheduled. Postmortem ticket opened.

Immediate mitigation steps (operator-first checklist):
1) Confirm scope: `kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels | grep -E "us-east-1a"` then cross-reference nodes with `kubectl get endpoints --all-namespaces | grep -A2 <service>` to see missing endpoints.
2) If node is "Ready" but endpoints are absent and tx_drop high: cordon node immediately: `kubectl cordon <node>` and start evicting non-critical pods: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (use conservative rate limit).
3) If CNI pod shows BPF/netlink errors: `kubectl logs -n kube-system daemonset/calico-node -l kubernetes.io/hostname=<node>` and check dmesg for netfilter errors.
4) Try soft restart of CNI agent on the node: `kubectl -n kube-system exec -it ds/calico-node -- bash -c "kill -HUP $(pidof calico-node) || pkill -f calico-node"` (if kube-api doesn't allow, use SSH to node and systemctl restart calico).
5) If conntrack exhaustion suspected: on node run `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` and if > 1.5M (cluster-specific threshold) run `sudo conntrack -F` only after traffic steering or cordon to avoid risky mass flush. Prefer increasing nf_conntrack_max via sysctl temporarily: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2621440`.
6) For kernel-level queues or XDP/BPF bad states, a node reboot may be fastest (coordinate maintenance window if stateful services present).

Commands we used during incident (copyable):
- List pods stuck Pending with events: `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o custom-columns='NAMESPACE:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,REASON:.status.conditions[*].reason'`
- Check calico BPF sync errors: `kubectl -n kube-system logs -l k8s-app=calico-node --tail=500 | grep -i bpf`
- Check kubelet->apiserver RTT: `kubectl get --raw "/metrics" | grep kubelet_*` (or use our apm view).
- Draining safely: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120`

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
- Primary: a kernel-level dataplane regression in the node image's BPF module (recent security backport introduced a change that, under high ephemeral port churn, increased packet drops and netlink error rates).
- Secondary contributing factors: conntrack table hit thresholds on nodes processing many short-lived connections (sidecarized proxies + LB health-check churn).
- Tertiary: scheduler/backoff behaviour made Pending-buildup worse because resource accounting snapshots were stale when apiserver reply times spiked.

Why this was novel/different from prior incidents:
- Nodes reported Ready (kubelet heartbeat persisted) so many automated checks didn't consider nodes fully degraded, leading to delayed automated remediation.
- The dataplane failure was asymmetric: inter-node pod traffic broken but kubelet<->apiserver path intermittently healthy, confusing health heuristics.

Runbook proposal (formalize into the SRE runbook):
- Add "islanded-node" state to node health model (Ready + dataplane_loss). Define dataplane_loss signals: tx_drop, conntrack saturation, calico BPF errors, interface errors.
- Automated remediation policy: when dataplane_loss persists >3m on a node AND pending pods on zone > threshold -> auto-cordon+evict (with controlled eviction caps).
- Avoid auto-flushing conntrack except in maintenance mode; instead prefer scaling load away then flush.
- If BPF errors present, prefer restarting CNI agent first; if that fails within 5m, escalate to node reboot.

Monitoring and dashboards to create/update:
- Node dataplane health panel (tx_drop, rx_drop, conntrack_usage, calico_error_rate) per-node and aggregated.
- Endpoint churn panel for services (endpoint disappear/appear rate).
- Scheduler backoff panel: number of pods in Pending with reason scheduling/insufficient resources over 5m.

Post-incident action items (with tentative owners):
- Confirm kernel backport regression with infra-image team and pin node image revision (Owner: Ravi Kumar, due 2025-02-20).
- Implement islanded-node detection rule and alert (Owner: Alyssa Chen, due 2025-02-28).
- Add safe auto-cordon+evict automation prototype to canary cluster (Owner: Jordan Miller, due 2025-03-10).
- Review conntrack default sizing for proxy-heavy workloads and publish recommended sysctl tune (Owner: Priya Shah, due 2025-03-05).
- Update runbook doc with step-by-step commands and add to on-call playbooks (Owner: SRE doc-owner, due 2025-03-01).

Open questions / followups:
- Is there a way to reliably detect dataplane-only failures without false positives from transient packet loss? Need threshold tuning.
- How do stateful workloads (databases) participate in automated recovery? Add annotation to skip auto-evict.
- Can we pressure-test the auto-cordon+evict logic in a chaos canary with controlled network partitions?

Notes to self (quick references):
- Slack: #sre-ops thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/CB12345/p1681234567890
- Postmortem ticket: SRE-1284 (linked above).
- PR with emergency config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-config/pull/342

Appendix: kubelet & kernel snippets observed:
- kubelet log sample: "E02011 03:48:03.123456 1 status_manager.go:156] Error updating node status: timed out waiting for the condition"
- dmesg sample from affected host: "NET_RX_DROP: netfilter: __bpf_skb_prog run failed rc=-22"
- conntrack sample: `conntrack -S` shows sockets=1492036, dropped=3820.

If you pick this up on-call: walk through the Immediate mitigation steps and then ping the infra-image owner before large-scale reboots. Keep a calm pace — avoid mass conntrack flushes without traffic steering.

End of scratchpad.
